From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@medisync.com>

Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo — evaluation alignments

Sergio / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier — appreciate the clarity on how Redwood approaches caching and fallback behavior. Quick summary from our side so we have a single list of decision inputs before we build the POC scope: 

- Primary pain: unpredictable inference cost and a variable latency tail that breaks clinician workflow during peak hours.
- Stakeholders: Pager/On-call (ops) care team leads, Security (infosec), and our ML infra team.
- Deal drivers: 1) Sub-second median response for short queries (<=128 tokens), 2) predictable cost at scale (forecastable monthly spend), 3) SOC2 / audit evidence for model access logs.
- Head-to-head: we want a focused smoke-suite to compare Redwood vs two incumbents on throughput, 95p latency, cold-start behavior, and token-level cost.

Open questions we need answered to write the test plan:
1) Can Redwood provide a small, reproducible test harness we can run in our environment?
2) What telemetry (per-token cost, per-request latency distribution, KV-cache hit rates) will be available during the POC?
3) Any architectural blockers for running a private VPC POC in our staging account?

We can carve out a two-week slot mid-July for the smoke tests; Daniel and I will coordinate infra access. Please confirm assumptions and what you need from us.

Best,
Alicia Ramos
Director of Product, Integrations
MediSync Health

Alicia — thank you for the clear list. Restating to make sure we’re aligned and to lay out next actions from Redwood: 

Summary (agreed pain/goal):
- Pain: latency tail and surprise unit cost during bursts.
- Goal: repeatable head-to-head that quantifies 95p latency, cold-start behaviour, and token-level cost at the traffic shape you’ll run (burst + steady).

What Redwood will deliver for the smoke-suite:
- A lightweight test harness (Python + k6 wrapper) we can run from your staging account. The harness includes: request generator with configurable sequence length distribution, KV-cache warmup script, and token-level cost exporter.
- Telemetry: per-request latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), per-token cost, KV-cache hit ratio, and per-request model variant used.
- Two test scenarios: 
  1) Steady-state 50 RPS for 60 minutes (to capture throughput + cost)
  2) Burst recovery: 400 RPS for 2 minutes then drop to 10 RPS (to capture tail/queueing)

Required from MediSync to run the POC:
- Staging IAM user with minimal compute access + a sample of 10k anonymized queries (we only need tokenized payloads).
- Confirmation if SOC2 evidence needs to be shipped (we can provide access logs and an audit bundle).

Proposed timeline / next steps: 
- By Mon 6/15: Cambridge team (Camila + Marcus) will share the smoke-suite spreadsheet and a short test plan. (Attachment: smoke-suite.xlsx — draft)
- By Fri 6/19: MediSync to confirm test slot (we suggested Jul 12–23) and provide staging access.
- Week of Jul 12: run test 1; Week of Jul 19: run test 2 + consolidation.

Immediate ask: Alicia, can you confirm the staging window and whether the telemetry needs to be ingested into your Datadog/Prometheus tenant or if a CSV export is sufficient?

Thanks — I’ll loop Camila for the technical test matrix.

— Sergio

Thanks — adding a few technical clarifications so the team can prepare the smoke-suite without surprises. I put the short matrix below and attached a longer checklist (redwood-smoke-tests.md).

Technical checkpoints (impact on measurables):
- Model variants: please confirm which model family you want to test (we suggest an Llama-2-70b-compat variant and a quantized 8-bit profile). Variant selection changes token-level cost by ~15–40% depending on sequence length distribution.
- KV-cache warmup: to measure realistic cold-start vs steady-state, we recommend a warmup of 5k contextual requests per keyspace. If you can provide a representative few hundred dialogues, that’s ideal.
- Network path: if you run the harness from your VPC we’ll instrument an agent; otherwise we’ll deploy a temporary runner in our Dedicated sandbox and you’ll observe from Datadog. Network overhead will add ~5–12ms median depending on region.

Suggested smoke-suite (high level):
- Test A: Latency parity — 1k short requests (<=64 tokens) against Redwood vs Incumbent-A & Incumbent-B. Measure p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1000-requests.
- Test B: Burst resilience — three 2-minute bursts at 300–500 RPS with 5-minute recovery windows. Track queueing and error rate.
- Test C: Cold-start delta — after 8 hours idle, measure first 200 requests to capture cold path.

Attachments included: redwood-smoke-tests.md (detailed checklist), poc-priority-matrix.pdf (decision matrix with weights).

Operational asks for MediSync infra team:
1) Provide an IAM user + key with S3 put/list for a temp results bucket OR grant us permission to push CSV to your Datadog.
2) Share a tokenizer sample set (JSONL) and expected sequence length distribution.

I’m around all week to pair on the harness. If it’s helpful, Marcus can take the lead on the k6 script and I’ll own the result parsing.

— Camila
Camila Reyes
